sensitivity_block.policy_variant: cache-enabled: 40% of T2 input at 10% of input price

rounding.notes: Applied at publication only; all intermediate arithmetic is full-precision decimal. basket_cost carries more decimal places than dated_siu so the published print is reproducible from its own published figures. siu_per_usd truncates so it never overstates the work a dollar buys.

correction_notes.note: A reasoning-token cost gap affected this print: gemini-3.1-pro-preview's reasoning tokens (RunRecord.usage.reasoning — real, captured in every run record for this print) were not priced. packages/print/src/compute/class-cost.ts computed cost from usage.output alone. Reasoning tokens are billed by the provider at the output rate — confirmed live, 2026-09-08: Google's own published pricing states "Output price (including thinking tokens)", and a separate live check (xAI's real per-call billed cost) independently confirmed the same billing convention for reasoning models generally. This is not a methodology refinement — the index measures realised cost from executed runs, and the run records already carried this field. Corrected figures, computed from this print's own real run records and price snapshot with the fix applied, not from new data: this print's dated_siu was originally reported as $0.0074; the corrected figure is $0.0084. gemini-3.1-pro-preview's own basket cost was originally reported as $0.013884; the corrected figure is $0.020744. This print itself is not recomputed or replaced — the original stands, per the revision policy's unconditional never-edit guarantee. The fix (packages/print/src/compute/class-cost.ts, cost-of-production.ts) applies forward from the next published print onward, which will show a real, one-time jump in gemini-3.1-pro-preview's cost for this methodological reason, not a market move — see docs/methodology.md's Index governance.

This print includes gemini-3.1-pro-preview, whose Google Cloud billing predates the point where it was isolated to this project alone. Before that, a real, unexplained cost gap was found between Google's actual billed Gemini cost and this project's own computed cost on every day independently checked (2026-09-08 through 2026-09-10 -- 2026-09-08 far larger than the others, but the gap wasn't confined to that one day). This project's own per-token pricing was independently verified against Google's real published rates and confirmed correct, ruling out a calculation error on this project's side -- but the cause of the gap itself was never established, and Gemini's own real invoice cost for any day before isolation cannot be attributed to this project with confidence. Because that evidence gap cannot be reconstructed after the fact, this print will remain status: "provisional" permanently, not through neglect. See docs/methodology.md's Index governance (§7) for the general policy and the isolation fix that resolves this for prints going forward.

Correction to this print's own correction note above: that note framed the real-vs-computed Gemini cost gap around Google Cloud billing "isolation," implying a shared project or key might explain it. That's now confirmed wrong. The Gemini API key this project uses (siu-runs-prints, created 2026-08-30) has been dedicated solely to this project's SIU print runs since its creation -- no other Google Cloud project has ever used it. There was no shared-billing contamination to isolate, and moving it to its own dedicated project changed nothing that needed changing. The real gap -- a real ~2.7x cost spike on 2026-09-08 against every neighbouring day, and a persistent mismatch against the real, dated exchange rate found on every other day checked -- remains genuinely unexplained. This project's own per-token pricing was already independently verified against Google's real published rates and confirmed correct, so it isn't a calculation error on this project's side either. This print's status stays "provisional" for the honest reason that a real gap's real cause is still unknown -- not because a diagnosed shared-billing problem was found and fixed, which the correction note above incorrectly implied. See docs/methodology.md's Index governance (§7) for the current, corrected state of this investigation.

Correction to this print's own two prior correction notes above: the first attributed a real Gemini cost gap to shared Google Cloud billing; the second retracted that as wrong but said the true cause remained unknown. Both are now superseded -- the cause is confirmed, and it is two distinct, real bugs in this project's own code, both now fixed forward (commit 48ba69c). (1) RunRecord.usage.cached_input was captured by every provider adapter but never priced by this project's cost formula -- a real, unconditional gap, not specific to Gemini. For this print specifically: gemini-3.1-pro-preview: 49095 cached tokens, $0.009819 -- together understating the published cost_of_production_usd ($0.8395) by $0.009819. This is not the hypothetical cache-adoption policy docs/methodology.md's sensitivity block already models (cachePolicyVariant) -- this cache use actually happened and was actually billed. (2) Separately, and the larger effect for gemini-3.1-pro-preview: the Google adapter (also the Anthropic and OpenAI adapters, structurally, though not yet triggered in practice for either) discarded a real, separately-billed API call's usage whenever Gemini's mandatory reasoning -- thinking cannot be disabled for this model -- consumed the whole completion budget and triggered an internal retry with a bigger one; only the retry's usage was ever recorded. This fires on nearly every gemini-3.1-pro-preview call, which is why Google's real per-day billed token counts (confirmed against the real Cloud Billing SKU breakdown) were consistently higher than this project's own recorded usage, including on ordinary days, and why 2026-09-08 specifically (and 2026-08-30, this project's first day) showed a real spike: this retry simply fired unusually often on those two days. Each affected run record's own deviations field carries the discarded call's real reasoning-token count; its real input-token count and full raw response were never saved, so this piece cannot be reconstructed precisely after the fact -- unlike (1) above, which is exact. Neither bug is corrected on this print's own signed cost_of_production_usd or dated_siu -- a published print's signed body is never edited -- so this print remains status: "provisional" permanently: bug (1)'s effect is now precisely known (above), but bug (2)'s cannot be fully reconstructed, so full retroactive reconciliation of this print isn't achievable. See docs/methodology.md's Index governance for the current, corrected explanation.

dated_siu previously rounded to a fixed 4 decimal places rather than 4 significant figures — found live and fixed the same day, 2026-09-25 (docs/methodology.md's Rounding section). At this print's price level that was too coarse to show real day-to-day movement. This print's signed body is never edited — the published figure (0.0074) stands. Recomputed from this print's own published basket_costs and weights (Σ weight × basket_cost, rounded under the corrected 4-significant-figure rule, reproducible by anyone from this print's own published figures alone), the real value is 0.007396.

Correction to this print's own rounding correction note above: that note's phrase "the real value is X" overstated what the recomputation shows. It restores rounding precision only — the precision a fixed 4-decimal-place rounding rule removed, recovered by recomputing Σ weight × basket_cost from this print's own published figures. It is not a claim that the recomputed figure is this print's true economic value. This print's own basket_costs are also affected by the reasoning-token and/or cached-input pricing correction disclosed elsewhere in these notes — usage that was under-priced before that fix landed — so the recomputed rounding figure is the unrounded version of a value already known to need that separate correction too, which this recomputation does not make. See docs/methodology.md's Rounding section for the general statement of this limit.
